That is a reason to gate exp89t, not a reason to reverse the user's build. Point (c) still holds: a 09:05Z submit comes before exp89r's read (L 9.30-9.48 h from 00:05:28Z = ~09:23-09:34Z), so exp89t would go in without any DIS evidence. fix: Keep the exp89t build and dummy gate (R22-A1 vs exp87a dummy CSV db3faf078781: nodes within +-1.5% of 122,328, COORDINJECT 4/4, change 0.60-0.69, 0 errors, RULE v2.1). When asking for the user's yes, offer a gated option (recommended): submit exp89t only after exp89r's first terminal header and only if exp89r is COMPLETE at >= 0.958 (the same rule (a) as exp89s). Then submit at ~09:35-09:45Z. The typical CI read lands ~18:55-19:15Z, before the 20:00Z tick. The ~10.9 h tail read (~20:35Z) would miss the tick, and on a late read exp89t is not a final (display only). Under the gate, exp89t (CI, the V_pub line) and exp89s (non-CI) fire on the same condition, so do not send both. Use exp89t in slot 1. Send exp89s in slot 2 only if exp89t's dummy fails, or if the user wants the non-CI DIS read as a clean attribution. If exp89r reads <= 0.957, ERROR or late, exp89t stays UNUSED. The ungated 09:05Z submit remains the user's call, but log it as an exception to winners-only.
realistic_gain: About 0 in expectation on private (DIS prior ~0: lab +0.0005 on K, -0.0007 to -0.0008 elsewhere). Public: P(display 0.960) ~0.3-0.45, mostly rounding. The gate mainly lowers the chance of a winner's-curse V_pub switch. It costs ~35 min of read margin before the 20:00Z tick.
